problem: The text says the age field 'is reduced as time passes', which is the older generic link-state convention. In OSPF, whose LSAs are introduced in Section 3, the LS age counts upward: it starts at 0 and reaches MaxAge (3600 s), after which the LSA is re-flooded and removed. A student may carry the wrong direction into an OSPF answer.
fix: Say it plainly for both cases: 'The age field is a timer. In OSPF the LS age starts at 0 and increases up to MaxAge (3600 s); when it reaches MaxAge the LSA is re-flooded and then removed, so a dead router cannot stay in the map forever.'

problem: The abbreviation ASBR is expanded as 'autonomous system border router'. OSPF documents and standard textbooks use 'autonomous system boundary router'. An examiner may mark the expansion as non-standard.
fix: 'An autonomous system boundary router (ASBR) connects the OSPF domain to an external routing domain.'
